clue.text: Pressure to publicise, backing movie about Shaft, say

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for an adjective: concerning the phallus

indicators.note: backing means moving rearwards, so the word for publicise is read from its end

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to air a view is to make it public
pic is informal for a film

explanation.surface: Promoting a revival of the 1971 detective film Shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaft is the private-eye film, but here it is the male member, and 'say' marks it as an example; Priapus was the Greek god of fertility.
explanation.definitionFit: Priapic means phallic, named after Priapus, so relating to the male organ suggested by shaft.

clue.text: Bulimic treated over single or multiple depressions

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so the eating-disorder word is reworked

blocks.note: the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient with bulimia being treated for one or more bouts of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the treated letters above the single I. The depressions are physical hollows, not low moods.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbilici is the Latin plural of umbilicus, the navel, a small hollow in the belly, so several such dents.

clue.text: Unknown garment hung up in the old cell

indicators.note: in a down clue, hanging something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top
the turned garment sits inside the archaic word for the

ye is an archaic spelling of the
a tog is an item of clothing, as in togs

explanation.surface: An unidentified piece of clothing left hanging in an old prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The cell sounds like a prison, but it is the biological one formed at fertilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A zygote is the single fertilised egg cell formed when two gametes fuse.

clue.text: Nothing by journalist is secured according to NBC?

blocks.note: zip is slang for nothing
per means by, as in per post
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter's story stays under wraps according to an American TV network.
explanation.walkthrough: NBC is an American broadcaster, standing in for American usage: zippered is the US form of the British zipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastened with a zip, as Americans say for a garment closed by its slide fastener.

clue.text: Formerly lascivious Liberal stripped old film-maker ...

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer covering, so the film-maker's surname loses both ends

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
Stanley Kubrick, director of 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: A once-lecherous Liberal undressed a veteran film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' tells the solver the word is archaic, not that the setter means an earlier state.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubric is an obsolete word for lewd or lustful, related to lubricious.

clue.text: ... turning, say, soon to embrace with desire

indicators.note: turning round means the abbreviation for say is read backwards
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the word for soon wraps round

blocks.note: early means before long
e.g. means for example, that is, say

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue before: the film-maker turning and soon embracing passionately.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link the surface to 5 down; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something eagerly is doing it keenly, with strong wanting or appetite.

clue.text: Lousy clubs introducing pack activity?

blocks.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
rummy is a card game played with a pack

explanation.surface: A poor nightclub scene leading into a wolf pack's hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' suggests wolves or rucksacks, but it is a pack of cards; 'clubs' too is a suit, not nightspots.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy, poor in quality, as lousy is.

clue.text: Roll into examination in court

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the bread item is placed within the test

blocks.note: a trial is a test or examination
a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: A list of names called out during questioning in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like a roll call, matching the court scene, but it is a piece of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that judges disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: In tense time, half-heartedly confirm stray stash?

indicators.note: losing half its heart means one of the two central letters of the word for confirm is dropped
in places the shortened word between the abbreviations for tense and time

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
to reassure is to confirm someone's belief
T is the abbreviation for time
to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: In a tense moment, nervously confirming where a lost hoard lies.
explanation.walkthrough: REASSURE has a double S at its centre; removing one of them is the half-hearted step.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is valuables found hidden with no known owner, a hidden hoard.

clue.text: Eccentric one wants only female underwear

blocks.note: a cam is an eccentric wheel in machinery
I is the Roman numeral one
sole means only, as in sole heir

explanation.surface: An oddball who wants nothing but women's lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as an adjective for a person, but it is the engineering noun: an off-centre disc on a shaft is a cam.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless top worn by women as lingerie.

clue.text: A lot of extremely lamentable rubbish getting rejected

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word
something rejected is thrown back, so the joined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: its outside letters
crap is vulgar for rubbish

explanation.surface: Much of some deplorable junk being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like 'much', but it is a lot in the auction sense.
explanation.definitionFit: At auction a lot is one item or bundle offered for sale, which is a parcel of goods.

clue.text: Spot independent returning in poll banning US state members

in places the reversed pair inside the shortened survey

blocks.note: a zit is a pimple
I is the abbreviation for independent
a census is an official count of people
taken as written

explanation.surface: An independent candidate rising in a poll that excludes one American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US state' looks like one phrase, but US is the letters dropped from CENSUS, while 'state' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens are the people who belong to a nation, its members.

clue.text: Bring back spun fabric in both hands

indicators.note: spun round means turned about, so the fabric word is read backwards
in places the turned fabric between the letters for the two hands

blocks.note: R and L for right and left
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Holding spun cloth in two hands to return it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spun' sounds like the making of yarn, but it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to summon back or remember, both senses of bringing back.

clue.text: Wee puzzle set by unfamiliar Scotsman

blocks.note: Jimmy is a form of address to a Scotsman whose name one does not know
a riddle is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: A small puzzle set by a Scottish stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' reads as the Scottish word for small, matching the Scotsman, but it means urine. Jimmy riddle is Cockney rhyming slang for piddle.
explanation.definitionFit: In British rhyming slang a jimmy riddle is a piddle, an act of urinating, which is a wee.

clue.text: Aromatic leaves spoil sweet butter

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart
a butter is something that butts, as a ram does

explanation.surface: Fragrant leaves ruin a dessert of sweet butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet butter' looks like unsalted butter; in fact 'butter' is one who butts, a crossword stock for RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is a herb whose fragrant leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Sydney's tearaway arriving, disrupting large international family

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into, so the arrival word goes inside the first abbreviation

blocks.note: L for large
arr is the timetable abbreviation for arrival
I is the abbreviation for international
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A young rowdy from Sydney turning up and upsetting a big multinational household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sydney's' marks the word as Australian slang rather than naming a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Larrikin is Australian slang for a hooligan or lovable rogue, a tearaway.

clue.text: Keen to contribute to live page about hired vehicle

indicators.note: contributing to something puts it inside, so keen goes within the verb for live
about means turned round, so the whole string reads backwards in this down clue

blocks.note: to be is to exist
acid means sharp or biting, as keen can
P for page

explanation.surface: An eager page boy helping out on a live broadcast about a rented car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is keen in the sense of sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw taken for a fare, a vehicle one hires.

clue.text: Search and rescue initiated by mostly vigilant island state

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for vigilant loses its last letter

blocks.note: SAR is the standard abbreviation
awake means alert

explanation.surface: A rescue mission launched by a largely watchful island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarawak is one of the federated regions of Malaysia, lying on Borneo, so an example of a state on an island.

clue.text: Much wine -- exceptionally clear bottles left

indicators.note: exceptionally means out of the ordinary way, so the word clear is rearranged
to bottle is to enclose, so the reworked letters hold the abbreviation for left

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
L for left

explanation.surface: A great deal of wine, unusually clear, filling bottles left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like the wine's containers, but it is a verb holding the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a stock of wine kept by a person or restaurant, so a large quantity of it.

clue.text: Latitude of capsized small boat -- longitude coordinate ultimately pinning it?

indicators.note: pinning something into it means fixing it inside the boat
a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue it reads backwards
ultimately picks out the final letter of the word coordinate

blocks.note: a yawl is a small two-masted sailing boat
E for east, a direction in which longitude is given
its final letter

explanation.surface: Charting the position of an overturned dinghy by latitude and longitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latitude' looks like the partner of longitude, but it means freedom of action. Leeway is also a boat's sideways drift, which suits the sailing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room for manoeuvre or freedom, as latitude is in the sense of scope allowed.

clue.text: Lesson hammered out amidst test

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so the next word's letters are reworked
amidst means in the middle of, so the reworked letters go inside the test

blocks.note: a trial is a test
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A class thrashed out in the middle of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session given by a tutor to a small group, a lesson.

clue.text: Perhaps hide artwork using rag as well

blocks.note: tat is tatty rubbish
too means also

explanation.surface: Perhaps conceal a painting using a cloth as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal, but it is a noun, skin; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a design inked into the skin, art on a hide.

clue.text: Old statesman to boast briefly, suppressing reserve

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for boast loses its last letter
suppressing keeps something held down within, so the shortened boast encloses reserve

blocks.note: to crow is to brag
ice is cool reserve of manner

explanation.surface: A former politician briefly bragging while holding back his reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was a celebrated Roman orator and politician of the first century BC.

clue.text: Vital our slips seek a win more than others?

definitions.text: seek a win more than others

indicators.note: slips means slides out of place, so the preceding letters are disordered

blocks.note: the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Our crucial errors make us chase a victory more than the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: to outrival is to beat in a contest, not just to seek a win.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrival is to outdo competitors, striving to beat them rather than merely compete.

clue.text: Shell swiftly locked on vehicle

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: A shell rapidly fixed onto a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locked on' places the word for swiftly attached after the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or similar creature.

clue.text: Papers are into where one can go around Oval?

definitions.note: the question mark marks oval as an example of egg-like shape

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for the toilet is read backwards
into means going inside, so the documents and the area unit enter the reversed toilet

blocks.note: the loo is the lavatory, where one goes
ID papers prove identity
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

explanation.surface: Documents are needed to reach a place where one can walk round the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here oval is just a shape. 'Are' is a noun, the metric area unit of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Ooidal means egg-shaped, from the Greek for egg, so describing an oval form.
